mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PLNC8 alpha/beta antiviral activity against enveloped viruses
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports envelope disruption as the main antiviral mechanism through Sytox Green permeabilization of LGTV, D-enantiomer activity arguing against a stereospecific protein receptor requirement, and rapid loss of infective virions after peptide exposure.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=17:Susceptibility of flaviviruses and SARS-CoV-2 to PLNC8 alpha/beta
source_locator.evidence: LGTV/KUNV results and Figs 1-4 support membrane permeabilization and virion infectivity loss.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct evidence is strongest for flavivirus permeabilization; SARS-CoV-2/IAV/HIV rows are infectivity readouts without equivalent direct membrane imaging in the extracted text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Liposome experiments support greater PLNC8 alpha/beta disruption of ER-mimetic low-cholesterol/anionic membranes than plasma-membrane mimetic high-cholesterol membranes, matching stronger activity against ER/Golgi-derived viral envelopes.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:The role of anionic charge in the outer leaflet and cholesterol content of phospholipid membranes in their sensitivity towards PLNC8 alpha/beta
source_locator.evidence: Results and Fig 10 compare ER-mimetic and plasma-membrane mimetic liposomes.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Liposomes are model membranes, not intact virions; do not convert this to exact virus-specific mechanism strength.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The article reports PLNC8 alpha/beta counteracted KUNV-induced cytotoxicity and peptide exposure did not cause cytotoxic effects up to 48 h in the tested cell context.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=17:Susceptibility of flaviviruses and SARS-CoV-2 to PLNC8 alpha/beta
source_locator.evidence: Results and Fig 6 describe LDH/cell morphology context for KUNV plus peptides.

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a local in vitro toxicity boundary; it is not a systemic safety claim.
